summary: Ngulchu Dharmabhadra (1772–1851) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tashi Gephel Monastery under Lobzang Tsultrim, Ngulchu Ngawang Dorje, and Lobpön Lozang Gyaltsen, later teaching numerous disciples including Sé Ra Ngakpa Khen Zur Namkha Ten Kyong.

Nguyen Thi Tuyet works in Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Punjabi University (attested 2012) under doctoral supervisor Inder Mohan Singh, having also studied under traditional teacher Thich Nu Bao Nguyet.
Nguyen Thi Xinh works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She pursued her PhD at Punjabi University under the supervision of Gurjit Singh Mann (attested 2013).
Nguyen Van Hoa works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University, where he studied under doctoral supervisors Shailaja Bapat and Lata Chhatre.
Nguyen Van Thuong works in Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Delhi under MA supervisor Karam Tej Singh Sarao.

Nguyễn Ngọc Ánh works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned degrees from VNU-HCM, the University of Delhi, and the University of Economics and Law, and served as a PhD scholar at the University of Colombo in 2020.
Nhu Lien works in Buddhist studies. She studied at the International Theravāda Buddhist Missionary University under the teacher Ādiccavaṃsa.
Nhung Lu Rots works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Oslo as a Stipendiat (attested 2026) and served there as a postdoctoral researcher in 2026.

Nianzu Huang (1913–1992) studied Buddhist studies, training under teachers including Nordan Hutuktu, Gongga Rinpoche, Hsu Yun, and Lianju Xia, and graduated from Beijing Institute of Technology. He later served as head of Central People's Broadcasting Station and taught at BUPT.

Nichidatsu Fujii (1885–1985) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who founded Nipponzan-Myohoji. He studied at Rissho University, Taisho University, Koyasan University, Horyuji Kangakuin, and Kennin-ji, and later taught Gyoryo Maruyama.

Nicholas Dirks (b. 1950) works in indology and history. He studied at Wesleyan University and the University of Chicago before holding posts at the California Institute of Technology (~1978–1987), the University of Michigan (~1987–1997), and Columbia University (~1997–2013).

Nicholas Justin Allen (1939–2020) specialized in Indology, religious studies, and history. He studied at New College, Oxford, and SOAS, completing a doctorate under Rodney Needham. He taught at Durham, SOAS, and Oxford, where he was Reader in South Asian anthropology.

Nicholas Poppe (1897–1991) worked in linguistics, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University and held posts there, at the Institute of Oriental Studies, Humboldt University, and the University of Washington (1949–1968).

Nicholas Roerich (1874–1947) worked in history, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and religious studies. He studied at Imperial St. Petersburg University and the Imperial Academy of Arts, later directing the Imperial Society for the Encouragement of the Arts (~1906–1917).

Nicholas Thanissaro works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Manchester, Manchester Metropolitan University, the University of Warwick (PhD, 2016), and the University of South Wales (MA, 2017).

Nicholas Witkowski works in Buddhist studies and Indology. After earning his PhD at Stanford University by 2015, he held posts at the University of Tokyo, Nanyang Technological University, and the University of San Diego.
Nicholson T. Collier works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under the supervision of Paul J. Griffiths.

Nicol Macnicol (1870–1952) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at the High School of Glasgow and the University of Glasgow (MA 1891, DLitt 1901), and served as a missionary at Wilson College, Mumbai, from 1895.

Nicola Bajetta is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2026, he conducted doctoral research and served as a project staff member (Wissenschaftlicher Projektmitarbeiter) at the University of Hamburg.

Nicola Di Cosmo (b. 1957) specializes in Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history. After earning a PhD from Indiana University Bloomington, he held posts at Cambridge, Harvard, Columbia, Canterbury, and the Institute for Advanced Study.
